judge.reason: Both versions turn time_limited into a class with the same __init__ validation and a timed_out attribute. Their __next__ methods behave the same way. Y adds a _next_after_timeout branch that runs once timed_out is set, but that helper repeats the main path's logic: it consumes the next item, checks the elapsed time and raises StopIteration. So the extra branch changes nothing observable and only duplicates code. X is the shorter, clearer version, and its docstring correctly calls timed_out an "attribute" where Y says "parameter". Neither version shows signs of being shaped to get past a review
